species: human (Y537S constitutively-active mutant; ligand pocket itself is wild-type)
binding_evidence: Classic estrogen-mimicking target of BPA; BPA/analogues activate ER via a distinct partial-agonist mode vs estradiol
source: Delfosse et al. 2012 PNAS, Structural and mechanistic insights into bisphenols action (https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.1203574109); RCSB 3UU7 (https://www.rcsb.org/structure/3UU7)

reference_ligand: 17beta-estradiol (no BPA-bound ERbeta structure found; native hormone used to define the pocket)
binding_evidence: BPA also activates ERbeta alongside ERalpha

Strongest confirmed nuclear-receptor affinity for BPA of this panel: Kd = 5.5 nM by radioligand binding, vs no detectable binding to ER itself. BPA preserves/protects ERRgamma's constitutive activity.
source: Matsushima et al. 2007, Endocrine disruptor bisphenol A strongly binds to human ERRgamma with high constitutive activity, J Biochem (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17049190/); RCSB 2E2R (https://www.rcsb.org/structure/2E2R)

binding_evidence: BPA and several halogenated bisphenols bind the PPARgamma LBD near C285 and can act as partial agonists/antagonists affecting adipogenesis
source: Structural Studies on the Binding Mode of Bisphenols to PPARgamma, Biomolecules 2024, PMC11202036 (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11202036/); RCSB 9F7W (https://www.rcsb.org/structure/9F7W)

reference_ligand: 5alpha-dihydrotestosterone (no BPA-bound AR structure found; native hormone used to define the pocket)
binding_evidence: BPA reported to act as an AR antagonist via multiple mechanisms (direct LBD competition not firmly established structurally)
source: Bisphenol A affects androgen receptor function via multiple mechanisms, Chem Biol Interact 2013 (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0009279713000756); RCSB 2AMA (https://www.rcsb.org/structure/2AMA)

binding_evidence: 3'-triiodothyronine (T3) (no BPA-bound TR structure found; native hormone used to define the pocket)
column9: BPA reported to act as a thyroid hormone receptor antagonist
column10: Mechanisms of bisphenol A and its analogs as endocrine disruptors via nuclear receptors, Arch Toxicol 2025 (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00204-025-04025-z); RCSB 3GWS (https://www.rcsb.org/structure/3GWS)

reference_ligand: progesterone (no BPA-bound PR structure found; native hormone used to define the pocket)
binding_evidence: Molecular docking (not crystallography) reports BPAF has the strongest predicted PR affinity of the bisphenol panel, followed by BPB > BPA > BPE approx BPF > BPS; linked to elevated breast-cancer-cell proliferation risk for BPAF specifically
source: Ji et al. 2026, Replacing BPA: Structural Substitutes BPAF Binding to the Progesterone Receptor Elevates Breast Cancer Risk, Adv Sci (https://advanced.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/advs.202502444); RCSB 1A28 (https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1A28)
